title: Reserved-throughput metering, burst accounting, and SLA credit reconciliation for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Design and implement end-to-end metering and billing logic for Redwood Dedicated customers. Scope covers: accurate accounting of reserved throughput (committed capacity) over time windows, bounded burst consumption semantics and how bursts are billed, rate-limiting interactions with reserved vs burst usage, SLA credit detection and automated reconciliation, and audit-grade telemetry for invoices. Goal is parity between what customers see in Console usage dashboards, what invoices charge, and the runtime enforcement behavior (throttling/fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Committed throughput consumption is recorded per-customer per-minute and reconciles with console rollups within 1% over a 24h window.
Burst usage is tracked separately with clear attribution (burst vs reserved) and billed at configured burst-rate rules.
Rate limiter uses the same counters as billing pipeline so throttling does not result in double-counting or missed chargeable tokens.
SLA credit generation triggers when monthly P99 latency of Dedicated pool exceeds SLA objective for a customer and produces an auditable credit entry tied to the invoice.
All accounting decisions have immutable evidence (event id + stored counters) retained for at least 365 days for audits.
Migration path for existing Dedicated customers with historical commitments: backfill reconciliation job can compute adjustments for invoices in the current billing month.
E2E integration tests cover normal, burst, fallback-to-hosted, and clock-skew scenarios.
Conservative rollout with feature flagging; telemetry shows no >0.2% deviation before GA rollout.
Security review completed for billing pipeline access to KMS and customer metadata (security_review_required=true).
work_log: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after PM spike; initial problem statement and scope drafted.
2026-02-23: Spike complete - identified two viable models for burst accounting (token-bucket meter vs prioritized queue accounting).
2026-02-27: Chose hybrid approach: token-bucket at ingress to enforce steady-state reserved throughput, plus a separate burst-meter that records overflow events for billing and throttling windows.
2026-03-03: Implemented prototype meter in staging runtime; observed 1.4% divergence with Console rollups due to minute-boundary rollups — root cause: inconsistent timezone handling in aggregator.
2026-03-05: Fixed aggregator timezone normalization and added deterministic minute-alignment function shared between runtime and billing pipeline.
2026-03-08: Cross-team review with PM and Console: agreed on fields surfaced in Console (reserved_used_tokens, burst_used_tokens, burst_overage_charges, sla_credit_reason).
2026-03-10: Added SLA-credit generator stub; needs production verification and legal review for credit calculation formula.
implementation_notes: Meter model: use per-customer sliding window of 1 minute (aligned to UTC minute boundaries) for committed throughput. Each request records token_count, timestamp, model_variant, route_id.
Reserved accounting: decrement minute counter from committed quota first. If minute quota exceeded, record delta to burst_meter but allow until burst_limit within billing period is reached.

Burst semantics: bursts are allowed to a configurable capacity (customer-tier dependent). Billing treats burst tokens at a premium rate; however, we keep separate per-minute counters so that short spikes don't immediately cause high charges without invoice-level visibility.

Rate limiter integration: runtime rate limiter should consult a shared fast-path counter (memcached or Redis) updated by request path. The same counter is the primary source-of-truth for billing pipeline via CDC (change data capture) events.

Billing pipeline: consume CDC from runtime counters, materialize per-minute aggregates in billing-store (time-series DB), and run invoice generator that applies reserved pricing, burst-price multipliers, and SLA credits.

SLA credits: computed monthly; when observed P99_latency > SLA_threshold and uptime < SLA_target, generate credit = min(credit_cap, missed_SLA_fraction * monthly_commit_fee). Store credit as invoice line item and as separate audit record.

Clock skew and reconciliation: include request ingestion timestamp and server_write_timestamp. Reconciliation job will prefer server_write_timestamp for aggregation; if delta > 60s, mark event for manual review.
Data retention: keep raw meter events (ids + counters) for 365 days. Aggregates for 3 years. All records immutable; corrections via compensating entries, never by mutation.
Migration/backfill: backfill job will reconstruct per-minute aggregates from raw events for last 60 days. For older invoices, produce adjustment reports rather than rewrites.

Testing: unit tests for counters, integration test with rate limiter, end-to-end test with synthetic traffic that simulates burst then equilibrium. Include fuzz tests for timezone/clock-skew and for fallback flows where runtime falls back to hosted model (billing should attribute to dedicated customer at burst price until fallback completes).
review_feedback: 2026-03-04 - PM (Linh Tran): Please ensure Console labels 'burst' vs 'overage' are unambiguous; customers should be able to distinguish allowed burst without penalty vs billed overage.

2026-03-06 - Security (Jonas Meyer): Billing-store access must be IAM-restricted and logs must be routed to audit S3; also ensure the SLA-credit generator cannot be triggered by arbitrary user metadata.

2026-03-09 - Finance (Priya Kapoor): Need specification of rounding rules and prorations for mid-month plan changes; add an 'adjustment_reason' field on invoice line items for customer support traces.
open_risks: Edge case: simultaneous multi-region failover could double-count tokens if both frontends record the same request due to retries; mitigation: idempotency key deduplication in billing ingestion.

Performance: per-minute atomic increments on hot keys (very large customers) could be a bottleneck. Plan: sharded counters with periodic merge jobs and conservative rate-limiter fallback when shard pressure high.
Legal/billing: SLA credit formula must be validated with Finance/legal to avoid unexpected liabilities.
Visibility: Console latency vs billing windows must be documented so customers understand why real-time Console numbers may trail billed totals by up to 5 minutes during heavy bursts.
next_steps: Complete PR implementing shared minute-alignment util and add it to runtime + billing pipeline (PR link in 'links').
Finish integration tests in staging and run 48h synthetic traffic campaign with multiple tiers (small, mid, enterprise) to validate rollups.

Plan feature-flagged rollout: 2 enterprise customers on private beta, monitor divergence metrics, then 25% of new Dedicated seats, then GA.
